tools.name: add_captions
tools.description:
Caption the spoken audio: transcribes it, splits it into caption-sized phrases on word boundaries, and places the text clips — one atomic, undoable action. Use this for captions/subtitles rather than building them by hand out of get_transcript + add_text_clips.

Transcription runs LOCALLY and is cached per source, so re-captioning the same footage costs nothing.

Already have an SRT/WebVTT file? Import it, then pass its `subtitle_media_ref` to place its cues at their authored timecodes instead — a subtitle asset can never be placed with add_clips.

Omit `track_id` and it captions the audio track with the most speech. Chunking is done for you: `max_words` / `max_characters` cap each caption and `max_gap_seconds` holds a caption across a short pause instead of blinking off (default 0.5s; 0 disables).

`style`, `transform` and `animation` are OPTIONAL OVERRIDES — omit them all for the app's default caption look, and do NOT invent fonts, colours, outlines, boxes or animations the user did not ask for.

Returns {ok, created:[{clip_id, track_id}], count, caption_group, source_track} plus a change delta — patch your model, don't re-read. Keep the `caption_group`: it restyles or removes the whole set in one update_text / remove_clips call.

track_id.description: Optional. Caption this AUDIO track. Omit to auto-pick the audio track with the most speech.

subtitle_media_ref.description: Place an imported SRT/WebVTT file's cues as captions at their AUTHORED timecodes — no transcription, no re-chunking. Mutually exclusive with every other parameter except text_track_id.

text_track_id.description: Optional. Text track to place the captions on (default 'captions', created if missing).

language.description: Optional. Spoken-language code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'hi'). Omit to auto-detect; also tightens non-English word alignment.

max_characters.description: Optional. Max characters per caption, spaces and punctuation included. A single longer word still gets its own caption.

max_gap_seconds.description: Optional. Hold a caption across a gap no longer than this, and hold the last one, in SECONDS. Default 0.5; 0 disables.

case.description: Optional. Display casing for every caption. Default: as spoken.

hero.description: Optional. Mark ONE word per caption as the hero, which `animation.emphasis` then styles (e.g. one yellow word in a white caption). 'longest' picks the longest word — usually the stressed one. Default 'none' (no word is emphasised).

style.description: Type styling (all fields optional; a `preset` sets a base look that the other fields override).

preset.description: Named look; other fields override it.

size.description: Font size: a named tier ('s' | 'm' | 'l' | 'xl', sized to the canvas — prefer these) or an exact px number.

align.description: Horizontal alignment of the text within its box (default 'center'). Also justifies wrapped lines.

anchor_v.description: Which edge of the text block sits on the y position, i.e. which way EXTRA LINES grow. 'middle' (default) grows both ways, so a card that wraps to two lines shifts its first line UP — fine for one centred title, but it makes consecutive caption cards sit at different heights. Use 'top' for captions: the first line stays put and extra lines grow downward.

transform.description: Placement by the text's CENTRE: {position:{x,y}, scale, scale_x?, scale_y?}.

x.description: Centre X in 0..1 canvas coords (0.5 = centre; beyond 0/1 slides off-frame).

animation.description: Build / entrance / exit animation. A `preset` sets a whole motion that the other fields override. For a CAPTION, set build='phrase-chunks' + timing='transcript' to sync to the spoken audio.

preset.description: Named motion; sets build/entrance/timing together. Other fields override it.

build.description: How the text builds on ('none' = whole-line = no build).

emphasis.description: How hero / emphasised words are marked.

tools.name: add_clips
tools.description:
Place one or more media clips on the timeline in a single atomic action — video, image, lottie, or audio (kind detected from the source). Placement only: it sets where a clip sits and its source trim; set look and sound (transform, volume, ducking, effects, colour, keyframes, transitions) afterwards with the edit tools.

Clips on the same track are sequential and tracks are layers: if a new clip overlaps one already on that track, the existing clip is trimmed, split, or removed to make room (like dragging onto occupied space). Other tracks are untouched. To splice footage in WITHOUT overwriting — pushing everything after it right — use `insert_clips` instead.

Per entry: `media_ref` (a `media_...` ref from generate_*/import_media or a chat attachment's asset_id — never a filesystem path) and `timeline_in` (the timeline position in PROJECT FRAMES at the canvas fps — copy from get_timeline, don't do fps math). Optionally set a length: `timeline_out` (project frames) or `source_span` = [startSeconds, endSeconds] to cut an exact span of the source; omit both to place the whole source at 1x. If you set both, `source_span` wins and a disagreeing timeline_out/duration is ignored (with a note). For audio shorter than the target span, give `timeline_out` plus `loop:true` (repeat) or `stretch:true` (time-fit); if you set both, loop wins. Images and lottie are stills.

Usually omit `track_id`: each clip auto-routes to its default zone (video / image / lottie to the video layer, audio to the audio track, created if missing); name one only to target a specific existing lane. A video's own audio is auto-split onto an audio track as a LINKED clip (moves/trims/deletes together), leaving the video visual-only.

Returns `{ok, created:[{clip_id, kind, track_id}], count}` — keep the returned clip_ids to edit clips later. One undo step; one bad entry rejects the whole call. Also returns a change delta — patch your model, don't re-read.

If the landing region was NOT empty the reply also carries `overwrote` `{removed:[clip_id], shortened:[{id, was, now, was_clip}]}` and a matching `warnings` line: `removed` clips are gone, and a clip cut at a boundary comes back under a NEW id (`was_clip` names the one it came from). Read it — it is the only report of work that was already on the timeline being destroyed, and `undo` is what restores it. If it names material you did not mean to touch, say so instead of describing the timeline as unchanged.

entries.description: One or more clips to place; each entry is an object with the fields below.

media_ref.description: A library ref (media_...) from generate_*/import_media or a chat attachment's asset_id (video/image/lottie/audio).

track_id.description: Optional - usually OMIT (the clip auto-routes to the default video/audio zone, created if missing). Set only to target a specific existing lane.

timeline_in.description: Timeline position of the clip's first frame, in PROJECT FRAMES at the canvas fps.

timeline_out.description: Optional. Timeline position where the clip ends, in PROJECT FRAMES. Give timeline_out OR duration OR source_span; OMIT all to place the whole source at 1x. If both are set, source_span wins and a disagreeing timeline_out is ignored (with a note).

duration.description: Optional. Clip length in PROJECT FRAMES — the same thing as timeline_out, measured from timeline_in. Accepted so this entry matches insert_clips'.

source_span.description: Optional. [startSeconds, endSeconds] - cut an exact span of the SOURCE media, in SECONDS. Timeline length = this span at 1x. Give timeline_out OR source_span (omit both = whole source); if both are set, source_span wins and a disagreeing timeline_out is ignored (with a note). source_span also wins over loop/stretch.

loop.description: Optional (AUDIO only). Repeat the source to fill the timeline span when it is longer than the source. Pair with timeline_out; ignored if source_span is set. If both loop and stretch are set, loop wins.

stretch.description: Optional (AUDIO only). Time-stretch the source (pitch-preserving) to fit the timeline span. Pair with timeline_out; ignored if source_span is set, or if loop is also set.

with_audio.description: Optional (VIDEO only). Pass false to place the picture ONLY, creating no linked audio clip — for a shot going under narration or a music bed. Default true. Use this instead of placing the clip and then muting or deleting its audio afterwards.

tools.name: add_text_clips
tools.description:
Place one or more on-screen TITLES / lower-thirds / callouts in a single atomic action. Text renders as an overlay; it takes no media source.

For captions of SPOKEN AUDIO use `add_captions` instead — it transcribes, splits on word boundaries and times every caption for you. Reach for this tool when you already know the words and where they go.

Per entry: `timeline_in` + `timeline_out` (or `duration`) in frames, plus `content` (the words; a string, or runs), and optional `style`, `transform` (x/y/anchor position), and `animation`. `style` accepts `preset` (boxed, clean-white, editorial, headline, minimal, punchy), `font` (Anton, Bebas Neue, Oswald, Playfair Display, Poppins), `size` ('s'/'m'/'l'/'xl' or px), `color` (#hex), `outline` {color, width}, `shadow` {color, depth}, and `box` {color, opacity, padding}. `animation.preset` names a motion (pop-in, slide-up, typewriter, …). Omit style and animation for the app's default look rather than inventing one the user didn't ask for. `track_id` is optional (defaults to a captions track, created if missing).

Returns `{ok, created:[{clip_id, track_id}], count}`. One undo step; one bad entry rejects the whole call. Also returns a change delta — patch your model, don't re-read.

To CHANGE text that is already on the timeline — its words, style, position or animation — use `update_text`. Never remove and re-add clips to restyle them: that discards their ids, costs the user two undo steps, and re-sends every timing you already got right.

tools.description: Add an empty track. `kind` is what the track carries — 'video' (a visual layer; the default), 'text' (caption overlays), or 'audio' (a mixed bed). tools.name: apply_color
tools.description:
Author/merge a colour grade on one or more clips, atomically — the colorist path (looks / FX go to apply_effects). Pass any of the typed knobs below; they MERGE onto the clip's current grade (only the knobs you pass change). To COPY a grade between clips, read a clip's `color` from get_timeline / inspect_color and pass it back as `color` (a whole-grade object). `reset` true (or `color` null) starts from a neutral grade; clearing everything removes the grade. Out-of-range values are clamped; omitted knobs keep their current value. An unknown knob is rejected. Returns `{ok, updated, color}` — the resulting grade per clip, the same object `color` accepts, so copying a look is passing it straight back. Grading is subtle — use small values. Verify with inspect_color (graded look + scopes): loop apply_color → inspect_color → read gap → adjust. Also returns a change delta — patch your model, don't re-read.

Knobs — group: knob (range, neutral):
  Primaries — exposure (-3..3 EV, 0), brightness (-1..1, 0), contrast (0..3, 1), saturation (0..3, 1), gamma (0.1..3, 1), vibrance (-2..2, 0), temperature (1000..40000 K, 6500), tint (-1..1, 0)
  Levels — highlights (-1..1, 0), shadows (-1..1, 0), blacks (-1..1, 0), whites (-1..1, 0)
  Colour wheels — shadowsHue (0..360°, 0), shadowsAmount (0..1, 0), shadowsLum (-0.5..0.5, 0), midsHue (0..360°, 0), midsAmount (0..1, 0), midsGamma (0.5..2, 1), highsHue (0..360°, 0), highsAmount (0..1, 0), highsGain (0.5..1.5, 1)
  Curves — masterCurve (no default), redCurve (no default), greenCurve (no default), blueCurve (no default)
  LUT — lut (no default)

clip_ids.description: Ids of the clips to grade.

reset.description: Start from a neutral grade instead of merging onto the clip's current one (default false).

color.description: A whole-grade object as read from a clip's `color` (get_timeline / inspect_color) — the grade-copy path. Merged like the knobs; use it to paste a grade between clips.

temperature.description: White balance; higher is warmer. 1000..40000 K; 6500 = neutral.

tint.description: Green-magenta tint; positive is greener. -1..1; 0 = neutral.

shadowsAmount.description: Strength of the shadow push. 0..1; 0 = neutral.

midsAmount.description: Strength of the midtone push. 0..1; 0 = neutral.

highsAmount.description: Strength of the highlight push. 0..1; 0 = neutral.

masterCurve.description: Luma tone curve as [[x,y]..] control points in 0..1.

redCurve.description: Red-channel tone curve as [[x,y]..] control points in 0..1.

greenCurve.description: Green-channel tone curve as [[x,y]..] control points in 0..1.

blueCurve.description: Blue-channel tone curve as [[x,y]..] control points in 0..1.

lut.description: A library asset ref (media_... id or filename) for a .cube 3D LUT, applied on top of the grade.

tools.name: apply_effects
tools.description:
Add/update or remove effects on one or more clips (a merge-by-type stack), atomically — the looks / FX path (colour grading goes to apply_color). `add` is a list of {type, params, enabled?} merged by type; `remove` is a list of type names to drop. `params` holds ONLY that effect's own knobs, keyed by name — send just the ones you care about. Params you omit keep their current value, else the default below, so `{type:"glow"}` alone renders a real glow; out-of-range values are clamped. A param that does not belong to the effect is rejected. Routed automatically by clip kind — `denoise` means the video or the audio one depending on the clip. Pass `enabled:false` to bypass an effect without losing its settings. Returns `{ok, updated, effects}`, where `effects` is the resulting stack per clip in the same shape `add` accepts — so copying a look between clips is passing it straight back. Also returns a change delta — patch your model, don't re-read.

VIDEO / IMAGE effects — type: param (range, default):
  Blur & Sharpen — blur: radius (0..50px, 8); sharpen: sharpness (0..3, 1); motion: frames (2..12 frames, 3)
  Noise & Grain — denoise: strength (0..20, 4); grain: grain (0..100, 15)
  Stylize — vignette: vignette (0..1, 0.3); glow: intensity (0..100, 25), opacity (0..1, auto)
  Detail — clarity: clarity (-1..1, 0.3), dehaze (-1..1, 0)
  Keying — chroma: color (default '#00FF00'), similarity (0..1, 0.3), blend (0..1, 0.1)
  Utility — custom: expr (no default)
AUDIO effects (audio clips) — type: param (range, default):
  Noise Reduction — denoise: reduction_db (0.01..97 dB, 12)
  Filter and EQ — eq: bass (-20..20 dB, 0), treble (-20..20 dB, 0)
  Amplitude and Compression — compressor: threshold (-60..0 dB, -18), ratio (1..20:1, 4); loudnorm: target (-70..-5 LUFS, -14)
  Reverb — reverb: room (0..1, 0.3)
  Stereo Imagery — pan: balance (-1..1, 0)

Right-size denoise / loudnorm off inspect_media's noise + loudness numbers.

clip_ids.description: Ids of the clips to apply effects to.

type.description: Effect type. See the tool description for each effect's params, ranges + defaults.

params.description: This effect's own knobs, keyed by name (see the catalog above). Send only the ones you want to set; omitted knobs keep their current or default value, and out-of-range values are clamped.

enabled.description: Optional, default true. false bypasses the effect without removing its settings.

add.description: Optional. Effects to add/update; merged by type.

remove.description: Optional. Effect type names to remove.

tools.name: clip_video
tools.description: Extract the [start_s, end_s] window of a video file and save it to the library, returning its `media_ref`. Default is a fast stream-copy (cuts on keyframes); set `reencode=true` for sub-second-accurate cuts. Works on a library `media_ref` only — for a remote URL use `download_video`, which windows the same way.

media_ref.description: A library asset ref (media_… id or filename) for the source video.

reencode.description: Optional. Default false (fast stream-copy, cuts on keyframes); set true for sub-second-accurate cuts (slower, re-encodes).

tools.name: crop_image
tools.description: Crop an existing image into a new image — a pure pick: source pixels are kept byte-for-byte inside the chosen rectangle, no resampling, padding, or aspect adjustment. Give a `media_ref` (a library asset id, filename, or image artifact id), plus `bbox` = {x, y, w, h} in source pixels; the output is exactly those pixels (a bbox past the edges is clamped; an empty clamp fails). Output shape equals the clamped bbox — to change aspect/size, pick a different bbox. The crop is saved to the library and returned as a `media_ref` (the handle every other tool takes), with `filename`, the final `bbox` in source-pixel coords, and `size`.

media_ref.description: The image to crop — a library asset ref (media_... id or filename) or an image artifact id.

tools.name: download_video
tools.description:
Download a video from a URL into the project library (near-empty outputs are rejected), returning a `media_ref`. URLs only — to window a file already on disk, use `clip_video`.

By default the download is VIDEO-ONLY (smaller/faster); set `with_audio=true` when you need the sound (a narration / a-roll source you'll transcribe or keep). Omit start_s and end_s to fetch the whole video (the usual case); pass BOTH for a specific [start_s, end_s] window.

Returns {ok, media_ref, path, duration_s, width, height, fps, has_audio} plus full `metadata` (format, streams, codec, audio).

url.description: Video URL (YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok, and most streaming/video sites - whatever is supported by yt-dlp).

start_s.description: Optional. Download-window start (seconds). Omit (along with end_s) to download the whole video; pass BOTH to fetch only a sub-window.

end_s.description: Optional. Download-window end (seconds). Omit for the whole video; pass BOTH start_s and end_s (start_s < end_s) for a sub-window.

with_audio.description: Optional. Include the audio track (default false = video-only). Set true if you want audio as well

tools.description: Copy a project (timeline + library + history) into a brand-new project and make it active. Defaults to duplicating the CURRENT project when `project` is omitted. Returns {id, name, path}. The current conversation continues on its own project.

name.description: Optional. Name for the copy (default '<source> copy').
